findings.detail: M3-S01-T4 already poses the same problem. In both questions a source states a value that conflicts with the value calculated from its own parts. In both, the answer is a stated value, a calculated value and a conflict_detected flag rather than forcing agreement, so the same reasoning leads to the answer. Option C (retry until the two values agree) repeats the earlier wrong option that retries until the total and the line item sum agree. Option B (keep only the calculated count) repeats the earlier wrong option that replaces the printed total with the computed sum. That is two repeated wrong options, more than the allowed one. Option D (switch to a strict schema) also echoes a wrong option in M1-S54-T1.

blind_answer.reason: Retrying cannot help when the source description itself states the wrong count. A conflict_detected flag records the genuine discrepancy instead of forcing agreement, and sending flagged PRs to a human reviewer resolves it. B hides the conflict, C wastes retries and could push the model to fabricate a matching value, and D only fixes syntax errors, not semantic disagreement.
